editorial:
Imagine being a Korean American kid in 1985 who just wants to fit in at school. That's Yong's world, and his escape is his idol, the world's most famous foul-mouthed comedian. When Yong makes a wish to become his hero, things take a wild turn. The movie mixes heart and humor as Yong suddenly finds himself living the life of his idol, complete with all the profane baggage that comes with it. It's a fun, nostalgic ride that captures the awkwardness of growing up and the pressure of trying to be someone you're not. The 80s setting feels authentic without being overdone, and the comedy lands more often than not.

The performances carry the film, especially the young lead who sells both the innocence and the chaos. The pacing keeps things moving, though some jokes repeat a bit too much. Still, the emotional core shines through, making it more than just a silly wish-fulfillment story. If you enjoy coming-of-age comedies with a nostalgic twist, this is a great pick.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Yong realizes that being his idol isn't all it's cracked up to be. The profane lifestyle starts to hurt the people around him, especially his family. The twist comes when Yong discovers that his idol was actually just as insecure and lonely as he is. Yong makes a heartfelt choice to be himself again, and his wish reverses. The movie ends with Yong embracing his own identity and making real friends at school, proving that being yourself is better than pretending to be someone else.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves coming-of-age comedies and 80s nostalgia.
